note.note:
History:
- Presenting complaint: Acute watery diarrhea for 3 days.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms began ~3 days ago with initial vomiting (a couple of episodes) that has now stopped; diarrhea has persisted and is ongoing.
- Frequency/character: Approximately 5–6 watery, loose stools per day; no visible blood.
- Associated symptoms: Initial feeling of feverishness/lightly warm, current marked weakness, decreased appetite, difficulty maintaining hydration because fluids precipitate more stools.
- Abdominal symptoms: Noted absence of significant abdominal pain ("not really").
- Triggers/exposures: No recalled recent takeaway or restaurant food; no known recent contacts with diarrheal illness.
- Previous episodes: None documented.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic illnesses: Asthma (uses inhaler infrequently).
- Medications: Blue inhaler — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: No known drug allergies reported.
- Family history: Father had hypertension and died of bowel cancer ~10 years ago; mother has type 2 diabetes.
- Social: Lives alone; software engineer; off work for past 3 days; non-smoker; drinks alcohol infrequently/socially.

Physical Examination:
- No formal vital signs or physical examination findings documented.
- Reported/observed findings from history:
  - Vomiting: occurred at onset, now resolved.
  - Diarrhea: watery, 5–6 times/day.
  - No visible blood in stool.
  - Reports feeling weak and initially warm; currently feels "kind of fine" regarding fever.
  - No headache or muscle pains reported.
  - No significant abdominal pain reported.

Impression:
- Most likely acute gastroenteritis (probable viral "tummy bug").

Management Plan:
- Symptomatic treatment and self-care advised:
  - Increase oral fluid intake; use oral rehydration solution recommended (Dioralyte) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Paracetamol advised if feeling feverish or to relieve malaise — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Work advice: Remain off work until symptom resolution; return to work when diarrhea-free for 24–48 hours.
- Safety-netting/follow-up: If symptoms persist/not improved by next week, return for reassessment.
- No investigations or prescriptions documented during this consult.

Patient Summary:
- Patient developed vomiting followed by 3 days of watery diarrhea (~5–6 episodes/day) with weakness and difficulty staying hydrated. The clinical impression is acute gastroenteritis. He was advised to rehydrate (oral rehydration solution), take paracetamol if feverish, stay off work until symptom-free for 24–48 hours, and return if not improved within one week.

Key Takeaways:
- Drink plenty of fluids; consider oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte).
- Take paracetamol if feverish or to relieve symptoms.
- Remain off work until diarrhea has been absent for 24–48 hours.

Next Steps:
- No immediate investigations or prescriptions ordered in this visit.
- Return for clinical review if not improved by one week.
- Return sooner if symptoms worsen (patient instructed to call back if concerned).

- Internal conflicts from transcript: none identified.
